Maya: Okay, thanks everyone. The main thing I want to understand today is how appointments are handled now and what you actually want the new system to change. We don't need to solve everything today.

Sarah: Yeah. The biggest issue is basically bookings. Right now customers either call us, WhatsApp us, or message Instagram.

Kevin: Mostly WhatsApp, actually.

Sarah: Yeah, probably WhatsApp now.

Maya: And then someone manually puts the appointment somewhere?

Kevin: We have a book at reception.

Sarah: And the Google Calendar.

Kevin: Well... not everything goes into Google Calendar.

Maya: Okay. So which one is considered the actual record?

Kevin: The appointment book, normally.

Sarah: Ideally both should match, but they don't always.

Maya: That's useful. What sort of problems happen because of that?

Kevin: Double bookings mostly. Someone replies on WhatsApp, another person answers the phone, and both give the same 3 PM slot.

Sarah: That's probably the main reason we're doing this.

Maya: So customers should be able to see available slots and book without contacting reception?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: But we still need to book appointments ourselves because some customers will always call.

Maya: Right. So both customers and staff need to be able to create appointments.

Sarah: Correct.

Maya: Walk me through what the customer needs to select.

Sarah: Service, staff member, date, time... that's probably it.

Nina: Branch as well.

Sarah: Oh yes, branch.

Maya: How many branches?

Sarah: Three currently.

Nina: Colombo 5, Rajagiriya and Nugegoda.

Maya: Could a staff member work at more than one branch?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: But not usually on the same day.

Sarah: Usually, yes. But sometimes they move if someone's absent.

Maya: So staff availability needs to depend on their branch schedule?

Sarah: Exactly.

Maya: What about services? Are all staff allowed to perform every service?

Sarah: No.

Kevin: Definitely not.

Sarah: For example, some junior stylists don't do colouring.

Maya: So when someone chooses a service, should the system only show staff members qualified to provide that service?

Sarah: Yes, that would be good.

Daniel: Just to clarify, is that mandatory for launch, or something we could add later?

Sarah: No, it should be there from the beginning. Otherwise customers might book the wrong person.

Maya: Got it.

Maya: How long is an appointment?

Sarah: Depends on the service.

Maya: Can you give me an example?

Sarah: Haircut, maybe 45 minutes.

Kevin: Men's haircut is 30.

Sarah: Right. Women's haircut is around 45.

Nina: Colouring can be two or three hours depending on what they're doing.

Daniel: Does the duration have to be fixed in the system?

Sarah: I think we should configure a standard duration for each service.

Kevin: But sometimes we need longer.

Maya: Would staff need to manually adjust the duration when creating a booking?

Kevin: That would help.

Sarah: Yes, for staff. Customers shouldn't change it themselves.

Maya: What happens after a customer selects a time?

Sarah: They confirm the booking.

Maya: Do they pay online?

Sarah: Eventually.

Daniel: Eventually meaning not version one?

Sarah: Actually... for expensive services we may need a deposit.

Nina: Colour treatments especially.

Maya: Do you currently collect deposits?

Sarah: Sometimes through a bank transfer.

Kevin: Then customers send us the payment screenshot on WhatsApp.

Sarah: Which is another headache.

Daniel: Are we saying online payment is required for the first release?

Sarah: I'm not sure yet.

Nina: We should probably check the payment provider fees first.

Maya: Okay. I'll leave online deposits as an unresolved item rather than treating it as a confirmed requirement.

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: Do customers need an account to make a booking?

Sarah: I'd prefer that.

Kevin: I don't know. Customers hate creating accounts for everything.

Sarah: That's true.

Maya: Could they book using just their mobile number?

Kevin: That would be easier.

Sarah: But then how do they see their previous appointments?

Daniel: We could authenticate using OTP.

Sarah: Like a code sent to the phone?

Daniel: Yes.

Sarah: That sounds better than passwords.

Maya: Are we agreeing that customers should use mobile number plus OTP rather than a traditional password?

Sarah: I think so.

Kevin: Yeah.

Nina: As long as SMS cost isn't ridiculous.

Maya: So technically preferred, but SMS cost needs checking?

Sarah: Correct.

Maya: What information should we collect from the customer?

Kevin: Name, phone number.

Sarah: Email.

Kevin: Most customers don't give email.

Sarah: Okay, email can be optional.

Maya: Anything else?

Sarah: Maybe birthday, because we send birthday offers.

Nina: We don't actually do that consistently.

Sarah: But we want to.

Maya: Is birthday required for booking?

Sarah: No, optional.

Maya: Let's talk cancellations.

Kevin: That's another problem.

Sarah: Yeah.

Maya: What happens today?

Kevin: They WhatsApp or call us.

Maya: How late can someone cancel?

Sarah: At least 24 hours before.

Kevin: But we let people cancel later all the time.

Sarah: That's because there's no system enforcing it.

Maya: In the new system, do you want customers prevented from cancelling within 24 hours?

Sarah: Hmm.

Nina: Maybe they should still be able to request cancellation, but reception decides.

Sarah: That's better.

Maya: So before 24 hours, customers can cancel themselves. Within 24 hours, they need to contact the salon?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: That works.

Maya: Rescheduling?

Sarah: Same rule.

Kevin: Actually, maybe rescheduling should be allowed until six hours before.

Sarah: Why would that be different?

Kevin: Because if they're still coming, just at a different time, it's less of a problem.

Sarah: But the original slot becomes empty.

Nina: Let's not make separate rules yet.

Maya: So cancellation and rescheduling policy still needs confirmation?

Sarah: Yes. Don't lock that one yet.

Maya: Do you need reminders?

Everyone: Yes.

Kevin: Definitely.

Maya: What kind?

Sarah: SMS.

Nina: WhatsApp would be better.

Daniel: WhatsApp integration may have additional setup and costs.

Sarah: Then maybe SMS first.

Maya: When should the reminder go out?

Kevin: The day before.

Sarah: And maybe two hours before.

Nina: Two messages for every appointment could get expensive.

Sarah: True.

Maya: So reminder channel and frequency need a cost check.

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: What does reception need to see?

Kevin: Basically the day's appointments.

Maya: One list?

Kevin: I'd rather see a calendar.

Sarah: Calendar by staff member would be useful.

Kevin: Yeah. Like columns for each stylist.

Daniel: Daily view only?

Kevin: Daily is most important, but weekly would be useful too.

Maya: Can reception move an appointment by dragging it?

Kevin: That would be nice.

Sarah: But make sure it doesn't accidentally change appointments too easily.

Maya: So drag-and-drop might be useful, but we'd need some kind of confirmation before saving the change?

Sarah: Exactly.

Maya: Should customers choose a specific employee or just choose anyone available?

Sarah: Both.

Maya: How would that work?

Sarah: They can select a stylist if they have a preference. Otherwise choose something like "any available stylist."

Kevin: A lot of new customers won't know the staff.

Maya: Makes sense.

Maya: Pricing. Is the price determined only by the service?

Sarah: Mostly.

Kevin: Not always.

Sarah: Yeah. Colouring depends on hair length and product usage.

Maya: Can the website show a fixed price?

Sarah: For those, it should probably say "starting from."

Daniel: Is the final price entered by staff after the appointment?

Sarah: Usually at checkout.

Maya: Does this booking system also need to handle checkout and payments in-store?

Sarah: Eventually yes, but I don't want this project to become a full POS system.

Daniel: Good.

Maya: So POS functionality is outside the initial scope?

Sarah: Yes. Definitely.

Maya: Do you want customer history?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: Appointment history would help.

Sarah: And notes.

Maya: What kind of notes?

Kevin: Things like colour formula, allergies, preferences.

Sarah: Be careful with that though because some information might be sensitive.

Daniel: We'd need access controls.

Maya: Who should be allowed to see customer notes?

Sarah: Stylists working with that customer and managers.

Kevin: Reception might need some notes too.

Sarah: Maybe not all notes.

Maya: Sounds like we need to define note categories or permissions later.

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: Can staff write anything they want in the customer record?

Sarah: Within reason.

Nina: We should probably have audit logs if someone changes important customer information.

Daniel: Which actions need auditing?

Nina: Changes to appointments, customer records, staff schedules... maybe cancellations.

Sarah: And refunds, if we add payments.

Maya: Okay. Audit requirements need to be defined in more detail.

Maya: How do staff schedules work?

Kevin: Usually 9 to 6.

Sarah: Different for some people.

Kevin: And days off.

Nina: Plus leave.

Maya: So managers need to configure working hours and unavailable periods?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: Also lunch breaks.

Maya: Should the system automatically prevent bookings during breaks?

Kevin: Yes.

Sarah: Definitely.

Maya: What about emergency changes? For example, someone calls in sick after customers have already booked.

Kevin: That's painful right now.

Sarah: We normally call everyone and try to move them.

Maya: Should the system automatically move their appointments to another stylist?

Sarah: No.

Kevin: Definitely not automatically.

Sarah: Reception should decide.

Maya: Could the system show alternative staff and time slots?

Kevin: That would be useful.

Sarah: Yes, suggestions are fine. Just don't automatically change customer appointments.

Maya: Notifications when staff change something?

Sarah: Customers should know if their appointment changes.

Maya: Immediately?

Sarah: Yes.

Kevin: Maybe only after we confirm the change.

Sarah: Obviously, yes.

Maya: So when an appointment change is saved, send the customer a notification.

Sarah: Correct.

Daniel: What about permissions? Are all staff using the same admin account?

Kevin: Currently, basically yes.

Daniel: We shouldn't do that in the new system.

Sarah: Agreed.

Maya: What roles do you expect?

Sarah: Admin, manager, receptionist and stylist.

Maya: Different permissions for each?

Sarah: Yes.

Daniel: Can a stylist see other stylists' appointments?

Sarah: Hmm.

Kevin: They probably need to.

Nina: Maybe only the schedule, not customer details.

Maya: That needs a permission decision.

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: Any reporting requirements?

Sarah: Definitely revenue reports.

Daniel: Revenue would require payment information.

Sarah: True.

Nina: For the first version, maybe appointment reports: number of bookings, cancellations, no-shows, busiest services.

Sarah: And busiest staff.

Kevin: Maybe customer retention too.

Maya: Do you have a definition for retention?

Kevin: Not really.

Maya: Okay, let's not invent one. We can define that later.

Maya: You mentioned no-shows. How are those recorded?

Kevin: We don't really record them properly.

Sarah: We should.

Maya: So staff should be able to mark an appointment as no-show?

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: And should anything happen automatically after multiple no-shows?

Sarah: Maybe require a deposit.

Nina: That's another policy we haven't decided.

Maya: I'll record the ability to mark no-show as confirmed, but automated penalties as unresolved.

Sarah: Correct.

Maya: Is there anything the system absolutely must not do?

Sarah: Don't automatically cancel or move appointments without staff confirmation.

Kevin: And don't let customers book a stylist who's not working.

Sarah: Yes.

Nina: Customer information shouldn't be visible to everyone.

Daniel: So we'll need role-based access control.

Maya: Anything else?

Sarah: I really don't want the system sending customers random messages because somebody accidentally edited something.

Maya: So notifications should only be triggered by confirmed appointment changes.

Sarah: Yes.

Maya: For launch, what would make you say the system is successful?

Sarah: If customers can book online and we're no longer double-booking people.

Kevin: If reception can see one reliable schedule instead of checking the book, WhatsApp and Google Calendar.

Nina: And if managers can control staff availability.

Maya: Okay. Those sound like the main priorities.

Daniel: One last technical question. Do we need to migrate all the existing customer data?

Sarah: We have customer details in different places.

Kevin: Some in Excel.

Sarah: Some in the old POS.

Maya: Do we know how much data?

Sarah: No.

Daniel: We'll need to inspect it before promising migration.

Maya: So data migration is not confirmed until we assess the existing data.

Sarah: Correct.

Maya: I'll summarise what we've confirmed and separate it from things that still need decisions. I'll also include the exact meeting statements so you can verify where each requirement came from.

Sarah: Perfect.

Kevin: Yeah.

Maya: Thanks everyone.
